name: Pin the statement before solving
cue: Any problem. Especially OCR text, OEIS offsets, informal wording ("distinct", "surrounded", "abuts").

name: Explicit counterexample
cue: "Every n ...", "the only solutions are ...", "X is always prime/composite", "no n with ...".

name: Scan a complete table
cue: Universal or uniqueness claims about pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers or sequence terms: "every Carmichael number ...", "the only ... are", "are there others besides ...".

name: Covering congruences
cue: "A·b^n + C is prime for some n", "for every x there is n with F(x, n) prime", families k·2^n ± 1, p + 2^n.

name: Congruence reduction to a constant
cue: "Infinitely many Carmichael numbers / pseudoprimes of the form p·g(p)".

name: Modular obstruction
cue: "X = Y has no solutions beyond ...", "every member of a family is a sum of ...".

name: Incremental SAT threshold
cue: "Least N such that every colouring / arrangement of [1, N] ...", existence of a small combinatorial object.

name: Finite verification of identities
cue: OEIS "Conjecture: a(n) = formula", "g.f. is ...", "satisfies the recurrence ...".

name: Parametric families plus a finite check
cue: "Every n ≥ N0 has a representation / two representations ...".

name: Density / union bound
cue: "Infinitely many n such that n − f(k) avoids P for all k", "every n is a sum of two numbers of type T".

name: Exact evaluation of real-valued statements
cue: Floors of roots, comparisons like n! vs m^m, "nearest x".

name: Units, Pell equations, continued fractions
cue: Sequences of n with a quadratic form value square ± constant; recurrences with palindromic coefficients; a(k+1) = a(k)^2 − 2.

name: Apply a classical theorem
cue: Coman-type "infinitely many pseudoprimes of form ..." claims and similar, where a classical construction already gives the family.

name: Direct elementary argument
cue: Anything settled by a short algebraic, combinatorial or number-theoretic argument not covered by another method.

name: Restatement, triviality, misstatement
cue: The item restates another one, is trivially true or false, or is misstated (OCR, wrong index).

name: Lean certificates in core Lean
cue: Any result whose evidence is a finite object or a finite computation, plus "for every n" claims reducible to finitely many facts and a periodicity lemma.

name: Layer LP with interval constraints
cue: Upper bounds for codes in hypercube-like graphs invariant under coordinate permutations, conflicts between nearby weights (Z-channel codes).

name: Asymptotics from polynomial recurrences
cue: OEIS "asymptotically", "a(n+1)/a(n) tends to", "mean of statistic ~ c n", "limit distribution is Poisson" for sequences with hypergeometric terms or P-recursive counts.

name: Creative telescoping certificate
cue: OEIS "Conjecture: (n+1)*a(n) - ... = 0" (P-recursive recurrence) for a(n) given as a finite sum of binomial or hypergeometric terms.
